title: K2 P2 ribbing
subtitle: The standard hat brim and sleeve cuff with a pronounced column.
excerpt: K2 P2 ribbing alternates two knit stitches and two purl stitches across the row. The wider columns give a bolder, more defined stripe than 1x1 rib and are the default brim in most standard hat patterns.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, Series 1 (1886). Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938).

glossaryTerms.definition: A rib pattern that groups two knit stitches and two purl stitches in alternating columns. The wider groups give a bolder column than 1x1 rib with slightly less elasticity but more visual weight.

content.text: K2 P2 ribbing (abbreviated k2, p2 rib) groups knit and purl stitches in pairs rather than singles. The wider columns in

give the fabric a more pronounced stripe and a slightly denser, sturdier edge than 1x1 rib. Because the yarn moves between needles only every two stitches rather than every stitch, it is also slightly faster to work. Difficulty: beginner.
A stitch count divisible by 4 (for flat 2x2 rib to align correctly on both sides)
Cast on a multiple of 4 stitches.
Row 1 (RS): (k2, p2) across, remembering to bring yarn forward before each pair of purl stitches and take it back before each pair of knit stitches.
Row 2 (WS): knit the knit stitches and purl the purl stitches as they appear.
Repeat Row 2 for the required length.

K2 P2 ribbing is the default brim on most worsted and aran weight hats. It provides enough substance to fold back into a double brim and stay there. Aran jumpers frequently use k2p2 rib on the welts and cuffs, where the bold column reads as part of the pattern rather than as a separate edging. In round knitting, the same stitch count rule applies: work (k2, p2) to the end of every round.

items.symptom: Columns do not line up on the second row
items.cause: Stitch count not divisible by 4, or row 1 started with p2 rather than k2
items.fix: Count stitches before casting on and confirm divisibility by 4. Begin every right-side row with k2.

items.symptom: Purl columns look wider than knit columns
items.cause: Working the purl stitches looser than the knit stitches
items.fix: Snug each purl stitch before moving to the next. The two purl stitches in each group need to match the tension of the two knit stitches.
